texts: A regurgitant area of 1.5 cm2 on an aortic prosthesis is not a normal finding: A.
Mechanical valves have small built-in washing jets that clean the hinges and keep clots from forming; they are short and narrow, with a pattern typical of each design.

A single central jet in a Medtronic-Hall valve, several small jets (often four) in a St. Jude bileaflet valve and two unequal jets in a Bjork-Shiley valve are normal, as is a short jet of about 2 cm on a mitral prosthesis.
A regurgitant area as large as 1.5 cm2 on an aortic prosthesis points to a pathological leak, through or around the valve, which needs further study.
In the picture, the robots' thin sprinklers are normal, while the robot in the orca's mouth floods back into the room.
Memory hook: thin sprinklers wash; a broad flood leaks.
